Invest Smarter: Properties at Fractional Costs! – Dauphin County, Pennsylvania Tax Deed Sale

Discover how you can snag incredible savings on properties through tax sales in Dauphin County, Pennsylvania. Participating in these sales can allow you to buy properties at 40-90% below their usual market price. Let’s dive into the details.

Dauphin County Tax Sales Overview

Upset Tax Sale: Held in September at the Crowne Plaza in Harrisburg. Register by mid-August with a $100 non-refundable fee. The highest bid wins, and full payment is required by the end of the sale day.

Judicial Tax Sale: If properties don’t sell in the Upset Sale, they may go to the Judicial Sale in May. This also requires a $100 registration fee, and the starting bid is set at $2,000, excluding current-year taxes.

Repository Sale: Unsold properties from previous sales are available here. Minimum bids start at $2,000 plus applicable fees, and bids must be written and approved by county authorities.

Pro Tips for Success

  • Perform a Title Search: Always research the property before bidding to avoid unexpected liabilities.
  • Understand the Sale Conditions: The county sells properties as-is, provides no warranties, and may include existing occupancy.
  • Prepare Financially: Ensure you have immediate access to funds for full payment on sale day.

FAQs

  1. What are the main types of tax sales in Dauphin County?

    Dauphin County conducts Upset, Judicial, and Repository sales. Upset sales occur in September, judicial sales occur in May, and repository sales are ongoing for unsold properties.
  2. How much is the registration fee?

    The registration fee for both Upset and Judicial Sales is $100, non-refundable.
  3. Can I finance my bid?

    No, buyers must make full payment by the end of the sale day. Buyers must make payments in cash or by check issued from local Harrisburg banks local Harrisburg banks.
  4. What happens when the county does not sell a property at the Upset or Judicial Sales?

    Unsold properties enter the Repository Sale, allowing buyers to submit written bids that county authorities must approveUnsold properties enter the Repository Sale, allowing buyers to submit written bids that county authorities must approve.
